speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with a low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and if anyone around you is currently sick?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19.

The clinical picture of a prodromal viral illness (fever, rhinorrhea) followed by a pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, culminating in a facial rash that spares the perioral region, is classic for Fifth Disease. Since the history is very specific, no further questions or tests are required to confirm this diagnosis.
